topic.title: Current version and new features
topic.p: This help describes Volkov Commander {{version}}. The program is based on Volkov's published 4.99.09 sources and adds F1 help, a modern build and small extensions. A final 5.0 release is being prepared; this development build is not that final release.
F1 opens help for the current dialog, viewer or menu. In the panels it opens the index. Enter opens a topic. Next and Previous change topics; Index returns to the list. Escape closes help.
F2, then F3 opens the extensions. They include archive menus, file lists, commands for selected files, format detection and a hex dump.

The directory/ZIP release includes downloaded DOS archivers. The 1.44 MB floppy contains VC and its own helpers, without those external archivers. The installer offers English, German, Russian, Polish and Slovak help.
The reference includes updated 4.99.10 menus, viewer keys, filters and settings. Unchanged operation descriptions are retained from the translated help; source provenance is recorded in SOURCES.TXT.

topic.title: User menus and new macros
topic.p: Press F2 for the user menu, then F3 for the extensions. F1 in the user menu opens the archive menu. Shift-F2 opens the main user menu when a directory has its own VC.MNU. Escape closes a menu; F10 inside an extension menu returns to the main or extensions menu as indicated.

VC.MNU and the other .MNU files are text files. Each item has a key and caption, followed by indented command lines or another .MNU filename. Installed user menus are preserved on updates. Add an addons.mnu item to an older VC.MNU to make the new extensions accessible.

! and !.! refer to the current filename without/with its extension. !@ names a temporary list of selected files. Without selection, VC uses the current file. The % forms refer to the other panel. !~.! and !~@ use short DOS names. ![Prompt] asks for input; !0 to !9 reuse answers.
New: !$ and %$ expand to VC's installation directory, with a trailing backslash. Use them to find helpers even when VC is not in PATH:

topic.title: Included archive programs
topic.p: The full release downloads and installs the DOS archivers beside VC. The menus use their installation paths. There is no need to find each program separately or add VC to PATH for the extension menus.

ZIP: ZIP.EXE / UNZIP.EXE are 16-bit Info-ZIP. A separate PKZIP menu uses the original PKZIP / PKUNZIP 2.50 shareware programs. ARJ: ARJ 2.78 Open-Source creates, lists, tests and extracts ARJ archives. ACE: ACE 1.2b is original shareware with a 30-day evaluation period. RAR: RAR 2.06 creates old RAR2 archives; evaluation is limited to 40 days. UNRAR 3.80 beta reads older RAR formats. Use Retro7Zip for RAR5 reading. LHA 2.13 handles LZH archives. ARC 6.02 and PKARC / PKXARC handle ARC.

Choose Create to pack selected files, List to inspect an archive, Test to check it, or Extract to copy its contents to the other panel's directory. Overwrite questions are still handled by the archiver.

Third-party licenses, manuals, complete original packages and required source archives are in PACKDOC. PACKERS.TXT lists versions and origins. These programs keep their own licenses; they do not inherit VC's BSD license.

topic.title: Retro7Zip and archive panels
topic.p: Retro7Zip 24.09+5 runs under DOS on a 386 or newer processor. 7ZA has the widest format support, 7ZR is smaller, 7ZM is for basic 7z files and low memory, and 7ZDEC is a minimal 7z extractor. Memory needs depend on the archive, compression dictionary and program variant.
The Retro7Zip menu creates 7z, ZIP, TAR and WIM files. gzip, BZip2 and XZ compress one input file; select only that file. Retro7Zip reads modern RAR, including RAR5, but cannot create RAR archives.

VCARCH.EXT connects archive panels to the appropriate programs. Enter opens a supported archive as a directory. F3 views a member, F5 extracts selected members, and copying files into a writable archive adds them. TAR.GZ and similar files have two layers: compression, then TAR.

VC7Z translates technical listings into VC's format, including solid archives. A solid member with no separate packed size shows 0 in that column. Missing dates use 01-01-1980. VC uses 32-bit file-size fields.

VC7Z also handles extraction to an existing folder and switches drives when necessary. It works around the DOS release's output-folder bug. Run 7ZA i for the complete list of readable formats and codecs.

topic.title: File lists and batch commands
topic.p: Open F2, F3, F4 for file lists and commands on selected files. N writes short names to VC.LST; L writes long names to VCLONG.LST; P writes full short paths to VCPATH.LST. B creates VCLIST.BAT with an ECHO line for each selected file. Existing output files are overwritten.
D previews a command for each file. R runs it. In the command, {} means the filename. The helper quotes each replacement. Example:

The preview executes nothing. Execution stops at the first failed command; earlier commands are not undone. Expanded commands may not exceed 126 bytes. Filenames containing shell control characters are rejected.

The lists are processed line by line. No extra recursive directory scan is performed by VCTOOLS. Relative names use the current directory. Use short-name lists for DOS file access; long-name lists are text output.
topic.pre: VCTOOLS list FILES.LST --full VCTOOLS run FILES.LST "ECHO {}" --dry-run

topic.title: Format detection and hex view
topic.p: In the extensions menu, T identifies a file by its starting bytes, not just its extension. It recognizes common archives, DOS/Windows and ELF executables, PDF, several image formats and WAV. Empty files and a simple text heuristic are also supported. This is not an integrity check.

H displays the first 256 bytes as hex and ASCII. The command line accepts an offset and a length. It is a read-only dump, not a binary editor or a complete Hiew replacement. Example: show 64 bytes at hexadecimal 100:

Z in the extensions menu lists a classic ZIP without an external packer. It reads the central directory; it neither extracts nor checks CRCs. ZIP64 and split ZIP files are rejected by this small reader. The Retro7Zip menu is available for its wider format support.
Command output can be redirected to a file with >. ADDONS.TXT contains the longer German guide to the extensions.

topic.title: OS/2 DOS-session helpers
topic.p: The full release includes the original AUTOINS.COM from the VC download area. It enables autorepeat of the Insert key in an OS/2 DOS session. Start it once per session from the OS/2 extension menu. The installer does not add it automatically to startup files.
OS2 contains the original icons: VC-WN.ICO for a windowed session, VC-FS.ICO for full screen, and additional VC icons. The original ZIPs are kept in PACKDOC/OS2.
These are helpers for DOS VC under OS/2, not native OS/2 archivers. VC itself retains its existing OS/2 extended-attribute support. Do not use version-specific patches for VC 4.00/4.01 on this build.

topic.title: Installation, updates and licenses
topic.p: Start INSTALL from the release directory. Select the target directory and the help language. Setup proposes a language from COUNTRY= in CONFIG.SYS. The selected help is installed as VC.HLP beside the program.

The full release asks you to accept all bundled archiver licenses before copying files. Nine dialogs cover VC and the third-party programs; some related license texts share a dialog. Declining cancels installation. Original terms, manuals and source packages remain in PACKDOC.
INSTALL /S uses GDI's unattended defaults and accepts the licenses automatically. Run INSTALL without /S for the interactive questions. The PATH entry and Windows Program Manager item are optional.
Updates preserve VC.INI and existing .MNU/.EXT customization. Existing menus may therefore need a new addons.mnu entry. INSTALL /U from the installed directory starts removal.
The floppy is the core package. Use the complete ZIP/directory release for the downloaded archivers, OS/2 helpers and their documentation.

topic.title: Current panels and settings
topic.p: The program uses the 4.99 panel system. Quick View previews the file from the other panel; it differs from the full F3 viewer. The current F9 menu offers display modes and settings inside VC itself.

Descriptions can be displayed in file panels. VC's existing description support is used; no separate FILES_NC or RESINFO TSR is required. Colors are also configured in VC; a separate VC-COLOR tool is unnecessary.
Use F9, Options for the current settings dialogs and Shift-F9 to save the configuration. The following reference chapters document the working settings dialogs and identify unfinished menu actions.
The translated keyboard, copy, move, search, viewer and editor reference pages are preserved after the new chapters in this help index.

When MAXTEXT is loaded, VC automatically selects its highest advertised text mode at startup: 80x50, then 80x43, then 80x25. This happens once per VC start. Without a compatible driver, sufficient startup workspace or an accepted switch, VC keeps its ordinary display. MAXTEXT is optional and is not installed or bundled by VC.

topic.title: Long filenames and DOS paths
topic.p: VC can use long filenames when the operating system or an installed driver provides the LFN interface. Under plain DOS, use an existing DOSLFN installation. No new LFN or NTFS driver is included here.
The new menus deliberately pass short names to small DOS helpers: !~.! is a short filename and !~@ is a list of short selected names. !@ can produce a text list of the long names known to VC.
Retro7Zip supports LFN through the available DOS interface, but the chosen archiver and filesystem still impose their own limits. A long filename does not remove DOS file-size or memory limits.

topic.title: Building and editing this help
topic.p: The .HLP files use VC's Norton Guides format. They are not Windows WinHelp files. The repository includes its own compiler, tools/hlp.py. No proprietary help compiler is needed.

All editable UTF-8 topics are in help/src/en.xml. Open the XML files in XMLmind; guide.dtd defines the structure and guide.css provides an editing stylesheet. SOURCES.TXT records the upstream help packages.
make help creates all five language files and the context map in build/help. The version comes from VcVersion in src/VCDATA.INC. For a help-only preview of the planned 5.0 text:

Use topic with a stable id, title, p, heading and pre. Inline b, u and code provide formatting. Keep topic IDs in the same order in all languages; help/project.xml maps contexts to IDs. The compiler wraps prose at 64 columns and checks DOS encodings and record sizes. Rebuild VC with its help after changing topic order or context mappings.

topic.title: About Volkov Commander
topic.p: Volkov Commander {{version}} is based on Vsevolod V. Volkov's published 4.99.09 sources. This repository adds a DOS F1 viewer, editable XML help, archive menus, helpers and a reproducible release build. The planned final version is 5.0.

VC and our source changes use the BSD 2-clause license. Downloaded archivers retain their own licenses. Read PACKERS.TXT and PACKDOC in the full release. Original help authors remain credited in the source guides.
Project: https://github.com/geosone/vc

topic.title: Keyboard reference
topic.p: Tab switches panels. Ins selects a file. Gray + selects a group, Gray - unselects, Gray * inverts selection and Ctrl-M restores it. Shift with the group keys also selects directories.

Ctrl-O: panels on/off; Ctrl-P: inactive panel on/off; Ctrl-U: swap; Ctrl-L: Info; Ctrl-Z: Tree; Ctrl-Q: Quick View; Ctrl-N: long names; Ctrl-R: reread; Ctrl-F: filter; Ctrl-A: attributes; Ctrl-B: key bar; Ctrl-Backslash: root directory.
F1 Help, F2 user menu, F3 View, F4 Edit, F5 Copy, F6 Move, F7 Make directory, F8 Delete, F9 menus, F10 Quit. Alt-F1/F2 changes drives. Alt-F7 searches; Alt-F8 opens history.

Ctrl-I inserts selected names in the command line. Ctrl-[ and Ctrl-] insert the left/right path. Ctrl-E/Ctrl-X recall commands; Ctrl-Enter completes a history prefix. These commands depend on the current panel and command-line state.

topic.title: Viewer keys
topic.p: Arrows scroll, PgUp/PgDn move a page, Home/End reach the beginning/end. Ctrl-Left/Right scroll horizontally by a larger step.
F2 toggles text wrapping; F4 or Enter switches text/hex. F5 goes to a hexadecimal byte offset in hex mode. F7 searches, Shift-F7 finds the next match, Ctrl-F7 the previous match.

F8 chooses a character translation table. Shift-F8, or Tab in the full viewer, shifts a DBCS character boundary. Esc, F3 or F10 closes the full viewer. F1 opens context help. Quick View uses a smaller viewer inside a panel.

topic.title: Viewer status
topic.p: The viewer status identifies the file and shows the column, byte position and percentage. Values change as you scroll. Hex mode displays byte offsets; its F5 Go to offset dialog expects a hexadecimal number.
F8 selects a character translation table for display. It does not convert or rewrite the file. The viewer is read-only; use F4 from a file panel to edit.

topic.title: Editor keys
topic.p: Arrows move the cursor, Ctrl-Left/Right move by words. Home/End reach line start/end; Ctrl-Home/End or Ctrl-PgUp/PgDn reach file start/end. PgUp/PgDn move a page.

Backspace deletes left; Del deletes under the cursor; Ctrl-Backspace deletes left by word. Ctrl-T deletes a word right, Ctrl-K to line end, Ctrl-Y a line; Ctrl-U restores deleted text. Ctrl-Q quotes the next character.

F2 saves; Shift-F2 saves under another name. F4 switches text/hex; Tab switches the hex/ASCII field in hex mode. F7 searches; Shift-F7 continues. F10 or Esc exits with a save question for changed files. Shift-F10 saves and exits. F1 opens help.

topic.title: Edit -- Status line
topic.line: ^bEdit (2/2) -- Status line^b
^uStatus Line^u
File modified ──┐
^rEdit: filename.ext *" Line 2 Col 3 449,268 Free ^r
Quote next char ───┘ Memory free ───┘

topic.title: Left and Right menus
topic.p: F9 opens the pull-down menus. Left and Right configure their respective panels. Choose Brief, Full or Description for file lists, Info for disk information, Tree for directories, or Quick view for a preview.

Long names (Ctrl-N) toggles long filename display when LFN services are available. Sort by Name, Extension, Time or Size, choose Unsorted, or toggle Reverse. Re-read, Filter and Drive apply to that panel. Ctrl-F1/Ctrl-F2 toggles the left/right panel.

topic.title: Brief, Full and Description
topic.p: Brief uses several filename columns. Full adds file size, date and time. Description shows descriptions read from the configured description files. Column layout depends on panel size and long filename display.

Hold Alt and type the start of a filename for quick search. Continue typing, use Ctrl-Enter for another match, or Esc to close search. Long names require an available LFN interface; Ctrl-N toggles their display.

Short-name case is controlled by Options, General, Show short names in lower case. Letter case alone does not reliably distinguish files and directories. Hidden-file indicators use the configured character set.

topic.title: Info panel
topic.p: Ctrl-L toggles the inactive panel to Info. It shows memory, drive capacity and free space, plus information about the directory in the other file panel. The values describe the running system, not fixed example numbers.

Directory text comes from the files listed in Options, Descriptions, Directory information files. Defaults include dirinfo, file_id.diz and readme variants. F4 in the directory-information area edits that text. Ctrl-R refreshes the panel.

topic.title: Tree panel
topic.p: Ctrl-Z toggles the inactive panel to Tree. Arrows select a directory; Enter changes to it. Alt and the start of its name open quick search.

Options, Panels controls Auto change directory and its delay, hidden subdirectories, and saving TREEINFO in the drive root or home directory. Ctrl-R rescans the tree. Use it after another program changes directories on disk.

topic.title: On/Off
topic.line: ^bOn/Off -- Toggle panel on/off^b ^uCtrl-F1^u, ^uCtrl-F2^u
^uCtrl-F1^u -- Toggle left ^uCtrl-F2^u -- Toggle right
This command toggles the left or right panel on and off:

topic.title: Sorting files
topic.p: Use Left/Right to sort by Name, Extension, Time or Size, or choose Unsorted. Reverse changes the direction. Sorting applies to that file panel.
Short names can be displayed in lower case through Options, General. With long names enabled, preserve the spelling supplied by the filesystem; do not infer the file type from letter case.

topic.title: Re-read a panel
topic.p: Ctrl-R refreshes the active panel. In a file panel it rereads the directory; in Info it refreshes drive and directory information; in Tree it rescans the directory tree.
Use this after changing removable media or modifying files with another program. TREEINFO storage in the drive root or home directory is controlled by Options, Panels.

topic.title: Filter
topic.p: Ctrl-F opens the panel filter. Select a predefined filter or enter a Custom filename mask. The Attributes area offers Archive, System, Hidden, Directory and Absent. Space changes an option; Ok applies it, Cancel leaves the dialog.

Filters control which entries are shown; they do not delete files. Predefined masks are read from VCFILTER.EXT. Use the long-name support chapter for LFN requirements instead of assuming every name is limited to 8.3.

topic.title: Choose drive
topic.p: Alt-F1 opens the left drive list; Alt-F2 the right. Choose a drive letter with the keyboard or mouse. For an unreadable disk, retry, choose another drive or cancel.
Show logical drive B: is in Options, General. It controls the logical second drive on a single-floppy system. This release does not require VCSETUP to change it.

topic.title: Files menu
topic.line: ^bFiles menu^b
The ^uFiles^u menu provides access to the commands on the
function key bar (in case you turned it off with ^uCtrl-B^u),
as well as some other commands that act on files and
directories, or that allow you to select groups of files and
directories.
^bNotes:^b
Some functions (View, Edit, Copy, Rename or move, and
Delete) have more general versions that you can
access with the shifted function keys. See help for
each command for details.
You can get the shifted versions of commands in this
menu by holding down the ^uShift^u key when you select
the menu item (with the keyboard or the mouse), or
using the shifted function key.

topic.title: User menu
topic.p: F2 opens the local VC.MNU if present; Shift-F2 opens the main user menu. Select an item with its key, Enter or the mouse. Commands can run programs or open another .MNU submenu.

The supplied main menu has archives on F1 and extensions on F3. A bound F1 executes that menu item; in a submenu without an F1 item it opens context help. Extensions include packers, lists and file inspection.
Edit menu files directly as text. Commands, Menu file edit is inactive in this build. See User menus and new macros for syntax and new !$ / %$ installation-directory macros.

topic.title: View a file
topic.p: F3 views the file under the cursor; Shift-F3 asks for a filename. F3/Alt-F3 internal/external behavior follows Alternative viewer in Options, General. Associations are read from VCVIEW.EXT, which can be edited directly as text.

The internal viewer supports text and hex, wrapping, character tables, byte offsets and searching. Esc, F3 or F10 closes it. The Viewer keys chapter lists the current keys. Quick View previews the other panel's file inside a panel (Ctrl-Q).

topic.title: Edit a file
topic.p: F4 edits the current file; Shift-F4 asks for a filename and can create a new file after confirmation. F4/Alt-F4 internal/external behavior follows Alternative editor in Options, General. External editors are configured in VCEDIT.EXT as text.

In the built-in editor F2 saves, Shift-F2 saves as, F4 changes text/hex and Shift-F10 saves and exits. F10 or Esc asks about unsaved changes. See Editor keys for navigation, deletion and searching. Large files may exceed the DOS editor's available memory.

topic.title: Copy
topic.line: ^bCopy^b ^uF5^u, ^uShift-F5^u, ^uCtrl-F5^u
The Copy command allows you to copy files and subdirectories.
There are four ways you can use this command:
You can copy the file or directory under the cursor
bar in a file panel.
You can copy a group of files and directories that
you've marked with the ^uIns^u key or ^uSelect group^u,
^uUnselect group^u and ^uInvert group^u.
You can type in the name of the file to copy (or a
group of files if you use DOS wildcard characters).
Press ^uShift-F5^u or hold down ^uShift^u when you select
^uCopy^u from the ^uFiles^u menu.
You can copy one file or directory under the cursor
bar even if some files and directories were marked.
Press ^uCtrl-F5^u or hold down ^uCtrl^u when you select ^uCopy^u
from the ^uFiles^u menu.
Pressing ^uF5^u (or selecting ^uCopy^u) brings up a dialog box like:
║ Copy "somefile.ext" to ║
║ [ Copy ] [ F10-Tree ] [ Cancel ] ║
There are three ways you can select where to copy the
file(s) to:
Type the name of the directory where you want to copy
the file or directory to (or the name of a new file
if you're copying one file).
Press ^uF10^u to bring up a pop-up directory tree of the
target disk and select a directory from this tree.
^uAlt-F10^u brings up directory tree of the current disk.
Set up the Commander so there are two file panels,
with the inactive panel showing the directory to
which you want to copy the files.
^bCanceling Copy:^b
Press ^uEsc^u at any time to stop copying files.
^bOverwriting or Appending Files:^b
If the target file already exists, you'll be asked to
choose overwriting or appending.
^bNote:^b File ^uTREEINFO^u will be rescaned automatically
after copying directories.

topic.title: Rename or move
topic.line: ^bRename or Move^b ^uF6^u, ^uShift-F6^u, ^uCtrl-F6^u
This command allows you to rename files and directories, or
to move files and subdirectories to other directories or
disk drives. There are four ways you can use this command:
You can rename or move the file or subdirectory under
the cursor bar in a file panel, or you can rename a
directory in a tree panel.
You can rename or move a group of files and
directories that you've marked with the ^uIns^u key or
^uSelect group^u, ^uUnselect group^u and ^uInvert group^u.
You can type in the name of the file to rename or
move (or a group of files if you use DOS wildcard
characters). Press ^uShift-F6^u or hold down ^uShift^u when
you select ^uRename or move^u from the ^uFiles^u menu.
You can rename or move one file or subdirectory under
the cursor bar even if some files and directories
were marked. Press ^uCtrl-F6^u or hold down ^uCtrl^u when you
select ^uRename or move^u from the ^uFiles^u menu.
Pressing ^uF6^u (or selecting ^uRename or move^u) brings up a dialog
box like:
║ Rename or move "somefile.ext" to ║
║ [ Move ] [ F10-Tree ] [ Cancel ] ║
There are three ways you can select where to move the
file(s) to:
Type the name of the directory where you want to move
the file or directory to (or the name of a new file
if you're renaming a file).
Press ^uF10^u to bring up a pop-up directory tree of the
target disk and select a directory from this tree.
^uAlt-F10^u brings up directory tree of the current disk.
Set up the Commander so there are two file panels,
with the inactive panel showing the directory to
which you want to move the files.
^bCancelling Rename or Move:^b
Press ^uEsc^u at any time to stop renaming or moving
files and directories.
^bOverwriting Files:^b
If the target file(s) exist, you'll be asked for
confirmation. You can choose between overwriting and
appending to files.
^bNote:^b File ^uTREEINFO^u will be rescaned automatically
after renaming or moving directories.

topic.title: Make directory
topic.p: F7 creates a subdirectory of the current location, or a directory at the entered path. A drive letter and full path can choose another location.
Plain DOS names use 8.3 limits. Long names require working LFN services and a supporting filesystem; see Long filenames and DOS paths. VC updates its tree information after creating directories.

topic.title: Delete
topic.line: ^bDelete^b ^uF8^u, ^uShift-F8^u, ^uCtrl-F8^u
This command allows you to delete files and directories.
There are four ways you can use this command:
You can delete the file or directory under the cursor
bar in a file panel, or the directory under the
cursor in a tree panel.
You can delete a group of files and directories that
you've marked with the ^uIns^u key or ^uSelect group^u,
^uUnselect group^u and ^uInvert group^u.
You can type in the name of the file to delete (or a
group of files if you use DOS wildcard characters).
Press ^uShift-F8^u or hold down ^uShift^u when you select
^uDelete^u from the ^uFiles^u menu. Be careful, though, as
you can delete a lot of files when you use the DOS *
wildcard character.
You can delete one file or directory under the cursor
bar even if some files and directories were marked.
Press ^uCtrl-F8^u or hold down ^uCtrl^u when you select
^uDelete^u from the ^uFiles^u menu.
^bRead-only files:^b
If a file is marked as read-only, you'll be asked for
confirmation before the Commander deletes the file.
^bHint:^b if you want to delete a group of files that are
marked read-only, use the ^uFile attributes^u command in
the ^uFiles^u menu to clear the read-only attribute
beforehand.
^bNon-empty directories:^b
If a directory is not empty, you'll be asked for
confirmation before the Commander deletes it. All
files and subdirectories in this directory will be
deleted then.
^bNote:^b File ^uTREEINFO^u will be rescaned automatically
after deleting directories.

topic.title: File attributes
topic.p: Ctrl-A changes Read only, Archive, Hidden and System attributes, plus date and time. For a single file, Space toggles an attribute. For groups, Set turns a bit on and Clear turns it off; leave both unchecked to preserve it.

Enter a date or time only when it should change. For directories, review the operation before confirming because contained files may be affected. The date and time format follows the DOS country settings.
Read only restricts normal writes; Archive is used by backup programs. Hidden and System also affect visibility according to the panel filter.

topic.title: Select groups
topic.p: Ins toggles the current item. Gray + selects by mask, Gray - removes selection, Gray * inverts selection, and Ctrl-M restores the previous selection. Group keys act on the file panel when the command-line state permits.

Use Shift with the group keys to include directories. A filename mask such as *.TXT limits a group. The exact match rules depend on short/long name handling; the old claim that all names are limited to 8.3 does not apply with LFN.
With Unselect during group operations under Options, Panels, completed items are unselected. This helps distinguish the remaining files after an interrupted operation.

topic.title: Quit
topic.p: F10 quits VC. Options, Interface, Confirmation on quit controls the confirmation question. Save manually with Shift-F9 or enable Auto save setup under Options, General.
Esc closes a dialog or viewer. Its behavior in the panels depends on Esc toggles screen on/off under Interface. A separate VCSETUP Exit command is not used by this release.

topic.title: Commands menu
topic.p: F9, Commands offers Tree (Alt-F10), Volume label (Ctrl-F4), Memory info (Alt-F5), Directory sizes (Alt-F6), Find file (Alt-F7), History (Alt-F8), EGA lines (Alt-F9) and Video mode (Ctrl-F9).

Ctrl-U swaps panels, Ctrl-O toggles them and Ctrl-C compares directories. Menu file edit is displayed but has no handler in this build. Edit VC.MNU and submenu files as ordinary text with F4 instead; see User menus and new macros.

topic.title: Change directory using Tree
topic.p: Alt-F10 opens the directory tree. Arrows, Home, End and PgUp/PgDn move through it; typing finds a directory. Enter selects it; Esc cancels. F2 rescans if the tree is out of date.

Options, Panels controls where TREEINFO is saved and whether hidden directories are included. VC updates its tree information for its own directory operations; rescan after changes made by another program.

topic.title: Volume label
topic.line: ^bVolume label^b ^uCtrl-F4^u
This command changes the disk volume label. The disk volume
label is displayed on the ^uInfo^u panel and when you use DOS's
DIR command.
Input up to 11 characters. You can use spaces and
interesting "high bit" ASCII characters. For instance,
you can set a volume label to:
^bSTARTUP 1^b or ^bHARD DISK^b
Press ^uEnter^u to confirm your input or press ^uEsc^u to cancel.
Input "empty" volume label to remove it from the disk.

topic.title: Memory info
topic.line: ^bMemory info^b ^uAlt-F5^u
This command lists the memory-resident programs which are
currently occupying system memory.
The ^uAddress^u column is the segment address of the start of
the program's memory block, in hexadecimal.
The ^uBlocks^u identifies how many blocks of memory are used by
the program.
The ^uSize^u column lists the sum of the sizes of all memory
blocks allocated by the program.
The ^uProgram^u column identifies the program if its name is
available, or specifies one of the DOS system area, Unknown
owner, or Free memory.
^uHooked Vectors^u lists the interrupt vectors which point into
memory owned by this program.
The resident programs which can be removed are marked by ''.
^bAction Result^b
^uCursor keys^u Use the cursor keys to scroll through the
list (use also Home, End, PgUp, PgDn).
^uIns^u Select/unselect a program marked by ''.
^uGray +, -^u Select/unselect all programs which can be
removed.
^uEnter^u Remove selected programs or a program
currently pointed by the cursor.
^bNotes:^b
TSR stands for Terminate and Stay Resident. This type
of program leaves all or part of itself in memory
when it returns control to DOS.
Often a TSR with a lower address controls interrupt
not listed here, but some other TSR (loaded after the
first) has seized primary control of that interrupt.
Most TSRs are careful enough to pass control to the
previous owner.
If a TSR was removed from memory, it often leaves a
large block of unused memory in low RAM. That memory
might be used by a smaller program, but it is not
available for a larger program. The solution is to
load such a TSR last, and remove it before loading
any other TSR.
You can remove TSRs which were loaded after loading
the Commander. To install the resident programs
automatically make a batch file, for example auto.bat,
including these TSRs and type it in command line when
the Commander starts:
VC auto.bat

topic.title: Directory sizes
topic.p: Alt-F6 calculates the total file sizes within subdirectories in the current panel. Values include files in nested subdirectories and may take time to calculate.

The sizes can be lost when a panel is reread. Options, Panels, Auto directory sizes enables automatic recalculation; Ins calculates size of directory can calculate a directory when marking it. These are logical sizes, not necessarily allocated disk space.

topic.title: Find file
topic.p: Alt-F7 searches for filenames and optionally text in the Containing field. Set the starting path and filename mask, then choose Find. Table chooses the character translation table used for the text search.
Stop stops a running search. New search starts another. Go to moves the file panel to the selected result; View opens it in the viewer; Quit returns to VC.

Use a path and mask to limit the search. The prefix *: requests all non-removable drives. Long filename handling depends on available LFN services. A content search reads file bytes and is not a search of compressed archive members.

topic.title: History
topic.line: ^bHistory^b ^uAlt-F8^u
This command brings up a list with the last DOS commands
that you have issued in this Commander session. Use the
cursor keys (or double click with the mouse) to execute one
of these commands again.
^bShortcut:^b To recall a recent command, you can type the
first few letters of the command and press
^uCtrl-Enter^u. For example, to recall the command
"word somefile.doc", type "wo" followed by
^uCtrl-Enter^u.
This shortcut recalls the most recent command
that starts with the letters you've typed.

topic.title: EGA lines and Video mode
topic.p: Alt-F9 switches between 25 lines and the higher EGA/VGA text-line count supported by the adapter. Ctrl-F9 opens Video Mode and lets you choose among available text modes.

The mode list depends on the BIOS and video hardware. VESA modes require VESA BIOS support and sufficient memory; an unsupported mode can fail. These are text display settings, not a graphical desktop.

When MAXTEXT is loaded, VC automatically selects its highest advertised text mode at startup: 80x50, then 80x43, then 80x25. This happens once per VC start. Without a compatible driver, sufficient startup workspace or an accepted switch, VC keeps its ordinary display. MAXTEXT is optional and is not installed or bundled by VC.

topic.title: Swap panels
topic.line: ^bSwap panels^b ^uCtrl-U^u
This command changes the position of the two panels so that
the left one appears on the right and the right one appears
on the left:

topic.title: Panels on/off
topic.line: ^bPanels on/off^b ^uCtrl-O^u
This command toggles both panels on or off. When both panels
are off, DOS's screen output will become visible.

topic.title: Compare directories
topic.line: ^bCompare directories^b ^uCtrl-C^u
This command compares the contents of the directories
displayed in two panels. Files found in one directory but
not the other are marked. Files that have been created or
changed more recently in one than the other are also marked.
If the two directories are identical, the Commander displays
a message about this.
To make two directories identical, use the ^uCompare^u
^udirectories^u command, then press ^uF5^u, ^uEnter^u in each panel to
copy the newer or unique files to the other directory.
^bMarks:^b
1. Files that have a more recent date than file in the
other panel.
2. Files that don't exist in the other panel.

topic.title: Editing user menu files
topic.p: Commands, Menu file edit has no handler in this build. Select VC.MNU or another .MNU file and use F4, or open it in an external text editor. Keep indented command lines below each menu caption. A submenu command names a .MNU file.

A caption can start with a key and colon, such as T: Detect format. Indent its command, for example "!$VCTOOLS.EXE" type "!~.!". Lines starting with an apostrophe are comments; @ suppresses command echo.

F2 uses a local VC.MNU when present; Shift-F2 opens the main menu. The supplied main menu binds F1 to archives, so that key invokes the item. Read User menus and new macros for filename, selected-list and installation-directory macros.

topic.title: Options menu
topic.p: F9, Options configures VC directly. General handles program execution and viewer/editor choices. Interface handles prompt, clock, mouse and display. Characters changes display symbols. Panels handles selection and directory trees; Descriptions controls description files; Copy and Move controls copy behavior.
Screen saver and the Extension file edit, Viewers and Editors menu actions are not implemented in this build. Edit the corresponding .EXT files with F4 or an external text editor.
Auto menus, Key bar, Full screen, Mini status and Memory allocation are menu switches. Shift-F9 saves settings to VC.INI. A separate VCSETUP program is not part of this release.

topic.title: General options
topic.p: F9, Options, General: Quick execute commands controls direct program execution; Command shell options sets shell arguments. Disable quick execution if it causes problems with a command.
Alternative viewer/editor swaps F3/Alt-F3 and F4/Alt-F4 behavior. External programs are configured in VCVIEW.EXT and VCEDIT.EXT; they must be installed separately.

Auto save setup preserves settings automatically. Show logical drive B: controls the logical second floppy drive. Show short names in lower case controls short-name display. Space changes options; Ok applies them; Shift-F9 saves manually.

topic.title: Interface options
topic.p: F9, Options, Interface controls Clock, Path prompt, Menu bar always visible, Alt alone selects menu, Esc toggles screen on/off, Clear keyboard buffer, Confirmation on quit and Error sound.

Screen colors offers Black & White, Color and Laptop. Screen output offers synchronized, asynchronous or automatic access for older adapters. Left-handed mouse swaps buttons; Fast mouse reset changes mouse initialization.
Zooming boxes animates dialogs; Zoom stages accepts 2 through 10. Space changes a switch, Ok accepts, Cancel discards the dialog. Save with Shift-F9.

topic.title: Extension associations
topic.p: Options, Extension file edit has no handler in this build. Edit VC.EXT directly with F4 or another text editor. Existing associations are still read. Keep the supplied syntax: a mask and colon followed by the program or indented command lines; apostrophe starts a comment.

Filename macros include !.! and the short-name form !~.!. !$ is the VC installation path; % forms refer to the other panel. External commands must exist on disk. See User menus and new macros for further substitutions.

topic.title: External viewers
topic.p: Options, Viewers has no handler in this build. Edit VCVIEW.EXT directly with F4 or another text editor. Existing associations are still read. Keep the supplied syntax: a mask and colon followed by the program or indented command lines; apostrophe starts a comment.

Filename macros include !.! and the short-name form !~.!. !$ is the VC installation path; % forms refer to the other panel. External commands must exist on disk. See User menus and new macros for further substitutions.
F3 and Alt-F3 choose internal/external operation according to Alternative viewer/editor in Options, General. The shipped association files refer to optional external programs.

topic.title: External editors
topic.p: Options, Editors has no handler in this build. Edit VCEDIT.EXT directly with F4 or another text editor. Existing associations are still read. Keep the supplied syntax: a mask and colon followed by the program or indented command lines; apostrophe starts a comment.

Filename macros include !.! and the short-name form !~.!. !$ is the VC installation path; % forms refer to the other panel. External commands must exist on disk. See User menus and new macros for further substitutions.
F4 and Alt-F4 choose internal/external operation according to Alternative viewer/editor in Options, General. The shipped association files refer to optional external programs.

topic.title: Auto menus
topic.line: ^bAuto menus^b
When this option is checked, the User menus appear
automatically when the Commander first starts. The User
menus will also reappear automatically after you run a User
menu command.

topic.title: Path prompt
topic.p: Set Path prompt in F9, Options, Interface. When enabled the command prompt includes the current directory; otherwise it shows the drive only. Shift-F9 saves the setting.

topic.title: Key bar
topic.line: ^bKey bar^b ^uCtrl-B^u
This option controls whether or not the function key bar at
the bottom of the screen is visible.
√ ^uK^uey bar ──── 1^rHelp ^r 2^rMenu ^r 3^rView ^r ...
^uK^uey bar ────
^bNote:^b With both the key bar and the panels turned off,
the Commander looks remarkably like DOS.

topic.title: Full screen
topic.line: ^bFull screen^b
This option controls the size of the ^uLeft^u and ^uRight^u panels.
When checked, the panels will have the height of the full
screen:
√ ^uF^uull screen ^uF^uull screen

topic.title: Automatic directory sizes
topic.p: F9, Options, Panels contains Auto directory sizes and Ins calculates size of directory. Automatic calculation may take time on large directory trees.
Alt-F6, or Commands, Directory sizes, requests calculation explicitly. Displayed sizes describe file contents; filesystem allocation and free space are different values.

topic.title: Mini status
topic.line: ^bMini status^b
This option controls whether or not a mini status line is
visible at the bottom of each panel. The mini status line
shows the full directory information for the file under the
cursor:
√ ^uM^uini status
║^rfilename ext^r│filename ext│filename ext║
║filename.ext 5728 5-15-91 6:44p║
^uM^uini status
║^rfilename ext^r│filename ext│filename ext║
║filename ext│filename ext│filename ext║
║filename ext│filename ext│filename ext║
^bSelected Files^b
If you select one or more files, the mini status line
changes to show how many files you've selected, and how many
bytes there are in the selected files:
║ ^b5,728 bytes in 1 selected file^b ║

topic.title: Clock
topic.p: Enable Clock in F9, Options, Interface to display the clock. Its time comes from DOS; correct the system time if necessary. Shift-F9 saves the display setting.

topic.title: Memory allocation
topic.line: ^bMemory allocation^b
This option selects the full-resident or small mode of the
Commander.
When this option is checked, the Commander deallocates
memory before execution of a program and loads itself again
when the program exits. It leaves in memory only ^usmall^u part
of the Commander.
Uncheck this option to set the Commander in ^ufull-resident^u
mode. So, you can execute programs quicker without reloading
the Commander each time. The program will have less memory
available to them, though.
^bNote:^b If you work in full-resident mode, use ^uShift-Enter^u
to execute a program in small mode without changing
this option. Hold down ^uShift^u when you select
command from the History or User menu.

topic.title: Save setup
topic.p: Shift-F9, or Options, Save setup, writes the current configuration to VC.INI. Options, General, Auto save setup enables automatic saving.

Settings include panel state and program options. Menu and extension files are separate text files. The VC environment variable can select a home directory for configuration files. Installation updates preserve an existing VC.INI; deleting it is not required for a normal update.

topic.title: Description settings
topic.p: F9, Options, Descriptions chooses whether file descriptions are not updated, updated only when displayed, or always updated during operations. Description files and Directory information files specify the filenames VC reads.

Defaults include descript.ion and files.bbs for descriptions, and dirinfo, file_id.diz and readme variants for directory information. Use Left/Right, Description to display file descriptions. Copy and Move has further options for creating and deleting description entries.

topic.title: Screen saver: current status
topic.p: Options, Screen saver is a visible placeholder without a dialog handler in this build. The old VC 4.05 instructions for its screen-blank delay and characters do not describe an available configuration dialog in 4.99.10.
Use Options, Interface for the working display and mouse settings. Changing this help text does not enable the missing Screen saver dialog.

topic.title: Characters
topic.p: F9, Options, Characters edits the symbols used for panel/dialog borders and pull-down menus. Other fields control scroll arrows, scroll bars, mouse pointers, progress bars, enabled items and hidden/selected file markers.

Choose characters suited to the loaded DOS font and codepage. Ok applies the dialog, Cancel discards it. Shift-F9 saves the configuration. This changes interface symbols, not filename encoding or the help language.

topic.title: Panel options
topic.p: F9, Options, Panels controls Ins moves down, Ins calculates size of directory, Auto directory sizes, Unselect during group operations and Highlight subdirectories for file panels.

Tree options include Show hidden subdirectories, Save TREEINFO in root directory, Save TREEINFO in home directory, Auto change directory and its time delay. With automatic change disabled, Enter selects the directory.
Space changes a switch; Ok accepts; Shift-F9 saves. Mini status is a separate switch in the Options menu. Rescan a tree with Ctrl-R after changes made outside VC.

topic.title: Choosing screen colors
topic.p: F9, Options, Interface, Screen colors selects Black & White, Color or Laptop. Choose the mode that is readable on your display, accept with Ok and save with Shift-F9.

The separate VCSETUP palette editor described by the old 4.05 help is not included in this release. The current Interface dialog selects a color scheme; it does not provide that old per-element palette editor.

topic.title: Copy and Move options
topic.p: F9, Options, Copy and Move controls Auto create descriptions, Delete target description if source without description, and Auto delete empty description files. Description processing itself is configured under Descriptions.

Copy extended attributes controls OS/2 extended-attribute handling where supported. Check target file and free space before copying enables advance checks. Clear read-only attribute when copy from CD-ROM prevents copied files from retaining the source read-only flag.
These options affect normal VC copy/move operations. External packers and VCTOOLS commands use their own behavior and options. Ok applies changes; Shift-F9 saves them.

topic.title: Country settings and codepages
topic.p: VC uses DOS country information for date/time and number formats. Set COUNTRY in CONFIG.SYS using files supplied by your DOS installation; choose the keyboard and display codepage with the matching DOS tools.

The installer uses COUNTRY to suggest a help language, but the selected HLP file has its own encoding: English CP437, German CP850, Russian CP866, Polish/Slovak CP852. A matching screen font is needed to display national characters.
Changing a translation table in the viewer changes that display only; it does not change DOS country settings or rewrite the file.

topic.title: Exit and retain settings
topic.p: F10 quits VC. Options, Interface, Confirmation on quit controls the confirmation question. Save manually with Shift-F9 or enable Auto save setup under Options, General.
Esc closes a dialog or viewer. Its behavior in the panels depends on Esc toggles screen on/off under Interface. A separate VCSETUP Exit command is not used by this release.

topic.title: VC Environment variable
topic.line: ^bVC Environment variable^b
Using the Commander with a RAM disk presents a special
problem: if you save the setup, change the main menu file,
or change the main extension file, these changes will be
made to the files on the RAM disk. As a result you'll lose
your changes as soon as you reboot or turn off your computer.
The Commander provides a solution to this problem. You can
put a line into your ^uautoexec.bat^u file that tells the
Commander where to find these files, as well as other files
it needs that you haven't copied to the RAM disk. Put the
following line into your ^uautoexec.bat^u file:
set vc=c:\progs\vc
The path on your hard disk where
the Commander's files are stored.
